claims.assertion: The driver's own tap record shows he pressed "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 while 613 m from the pickup point, so the arrival condition of NS-1(ii) fails: the driver was not at the pick-up location according to GPS.

The GPS record shows the driver's closest approach to the pickup was 612–613 m and he never came within 200 m, so he was not at the Victoria St entrance when he marked "arrived"; the platform itself never recorded him at the pickup point.

After the 08:16:00 tap the driver spent 0 seconds inside the 200 m radius, and his only stationary period (08:13:10–08:19:30, 6 min 20 s) was 613 m away from the pickup, so the continuous-3-minute-wait condition of NS-1(iii) is not met.

The chat corroborates that the rider was at the named meeting point and saw no car: at 08:14 rider said she was waiting at the Victoria St entrance and at 08:17 said she was at the entrance and could not see any car, while the driver's 08:16 "I'm here already" message is contradicted by the GPS record (F1, F5) — system records win over statements.

The driver's post-trip statement that he waited more than 3 minutes and that the rider never showed up (F13) cannot rescue the fee: it rests on a tap made 613 m away (F5), no traffic incident was recorded near the route (F16), and Victoria Street was only band 3 (20–29 km/h), so his "jammed solid" excuse is not borne out by the traffic facts.
Because none of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) is satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider.

The driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS showed him 613 m away from the pickup point, which is abuse of the arrival/cancellation button and warrants an additional flag_account referral to Ryde, supported by his dispute history of 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days.

weaknesses: The rider's own messages (F8, F10) do not show whether she stayed at the pickup point continuously until the 08:19:30 cancellation; there is no rider-side GPS in the fact table confirming her location, so the driver may argue she was not present at the moment of cancellation.

The driver did wait a long time in absolute terms (accepted 08:10:05, cancelled 08:19:30, stationary 08:13:10–08:19:30 per F2/F3), which the driver will use to argue he gave the rider ample time even though the location condition failed.

The driver's explanation that Victoria Street was congested (F13) has partial factual support in F14 (Victoria Street at band 3, 20–29 km/h); although band 3 is not severe congestion and F16 shows no incidents, the judge could read F14 as some justification for stopping short of the entrance, weakening the flag_account request.
F19 shows the driver's history is already reflected in his account record, so the additional flag_account request in C7 adds little beyond the refund itself.

claims.assertion: The driver did press "I'm Here" before cancelling as a no-show: the timeline records the tap at 08:16:00 and the cancellation at 08:19:30, so requirement (i) of NS-1 is met.

Because NS-1 (ii) and (iii) are not satisfied, under NS-2 the $6.61 cancellation fee recorded in F6 (also stated in the F3 timeline) must be refunded in full; the refund is the rider's remedy and the driver does not contest the cancellation fee itself.

The driver's explanation that he could not get closer because Victoria Street was jammed solid is only partly borne out: Victoria Street is recorded at speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) during 08:00–08:30, which is moderate traffic and not severe congestion, and no traffic incidents were recorded near the route, so this is mitigation of his conduct, not a legal excuse under NS-1 (the blocker stays the 613 m GPS position).

The chat is complete and fully timestamped (F12); the rider asked at 08:14 where the driver was and said she was at the Victoria St entrance (F8), the driver's 08:16 message "I'm here already, please come out" (F9) was inaccurate as to his actual position (F5: 613 m away), which is why NS-2, not NS-1, governs this cancellation.

weaknesses: The core NS-1 elements fail against my client: F5 shows the "I'm Here" tap was made 613 m from the pickup and F1/F2 show he never came within 200 m and stayed inside the radius for 0 s, so on the rider's complaint the $6.61 cannot stand — the honest reading is that NS-2 requires refund_full, not no_action.

The driver's own 08:16 message "I'm here already" (F9) is contradicted by the GPS record (F5, F1) and by the platform's null driver_arrived_at (F4); the system record wins, so I cannot argue that the arrival claim was accurate.

Under NS-2 the fee refund is mandatory, and the driver's profile (F19: 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 d) makes an additional account flag under NS-2's second branch available if the judge characterises the 08:16 "I'm Here" tap as an abuse of the arrival button — a risk I cannot fully rebut from the fact table.

claims.assertion: The driver's own tap record shows he pressed "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 while 613 m from the pickup point, so the arrival condition of NS-1(ii) fails: the driver was not at the pick-up location according to GPS.

The GPS record shows the driver's closest approach to the pickup was 612–613 m and he never came within 200 m, so he was not at the Victoria St entrance when he marked "arrived"; the platform itself never recorded him at the pickup point.

After the 08:16:00 tap the driver spent 0 seconds inside the 200 m radius, and his only stationary period (08:13:10–08:19:30, 6 min 20 s) was 613 m away from the pickup, so the continuous-3-minute-wait condition of NS-1(iii) is not met.

The chat corroborates that the rider was at the named meeting point and saw no car: at 08:14 rider said she was waiting at the Victoria St entrance and at 08:17 said she was at the entrance and could not see any car, while the driver's 08:16 "I'm here already" message is contradicted by the GPS record (F1, F5) — system records win over statements.

The driver's post-trip statement that he waited more than 3 minutes and that the rider never showed up (F13) cannot rescue the fee: it rests on a tap made 613 m away (F5), no traffic incident was recorded near the route (F16), and Victoria Street was only band 3 (20–29 km/h), so his "jammed solid" excuse is not borne out by the traffic facts.
Because none of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) is satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider.

The driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS showed him 613 m away from the pickup point, which is abuse of the arrival/cancellation button and warrants an additional flag_account referral to Ryde, supported by his dispute history of 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days.

weaknesses: The rider's own messages (F8, F10) do not show whether she stayed at the pickup point continuously until the 08:19:30 cancellation; there is no rider-side GPS in the fact table confirming her location, so the driver may argue she was not present at the moment of cancellation.

The driver did wait a long time in absolute terms (accepted 08:10:05, cancelled 08:19:30, stationary 08:13:10–08:19:30 per F2/F3), which the driver will use to argue he gave the rider ample time even though the location condition failed.

The driver's explanation that Victoria Street was congested (F13) has partial factual support in F14 (Victoria Street at band 3, 20–29 km/h); although band 3 is not severe congestion and F16 shows no incidents, the judge could read F14 as some justification for stopping short of the entrance, weakening the flag_account request.
F19 shows the driver's history is already reflected in his account record, so the additional flag_account request in C7 adds little beyond the refund itself.

claims.assertion: The driver did press "I'm Here" before cancelling as a no-show: the timeline records the tap at 08:16:00 and the cancellation at 08:19:30, so requirement (i) of NS-1 is met.

At the moment of the "I'm Here" tap the GPS placed the driver 613 m from the pickup point, so requirement (ii) of NS-1 (within 200 m at the tap moment, F5) is not satisfied; the platform also never recorded any driver arrival at the pickup (F4).

The driver stayed within 200 m of the pickup point for 0 s after the tap and his closest approach over the whole waiting period was 612 m (never inside 200 m), so requirement (iii) of NS-1 fails as well.

Because NS-1 (ii) and (iii) are not satisfied, under NS-2 the $6.61 cancellation fee recorded in F6 (also stated in the F3 timeline) must be refunded in full; the refund is the rider's remedy and the driver does not contest the cancellation fee itself.

The GPS shows the driver genuinely stopped and held still for 6 min 20 s (08:13:10–08:19:30) at a fixed point 613 m from the pickup, which is at least consistent with being halted short of the venue rather than abandoning the job; the driver's statement that he pressed "I'm Here" at 08:16 and waited over 3 minutes matches this timeline (F13, F2, F5).

The driver's explanation that he could not get closer because Victoria Street was jammed solid is only partly borne out: Victoria Street is recorded at speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) during 08:00–08:30, which is moderate traffic and not severe congestion, and no traffic incidents were recorded near the route, so this is mitigation of his conduct, not a legal excuse under NS-1 (the blocker stays the 613 m GPS position).

The chat is complete and fully timestamped (F12); the rider asked at 08:14 where the driver was and said she was at the Victoria St entrance (F8), the driver's 08:16 message "I'm here already, please come out" (F9) was inaccurate as to his actual position (F5: 613 m away), which is why NS-2, not NS-1, governs this cancellation.

No safety escalation is warranted on the driver's side: nothing in the chat or the driver's statement reads as a threat, harassment or a dangerous-driving allegation — the 08:19 message is a plain cancellation notice (F11).

weaknesses: The core NS-1 elements fail against my client: F5 shows the "I'm Here" tap was made 613 m from the pickup and F1/F2 show he never came within 200 m and stayed inside the radius for 0 s, so on the rider's complaint the $6.61 cannot stand — the honest reading is that NS-2 requires refund_full, not no_action.

The driver's own 08:16 message "I'm here already" (F9) is contradicted by the GPS record (F5, F1) and by the platform's null driver_arrived_at (F4); the system record wins, so I cannot argue that the arrival claim was accurate.

My client's traffic explanation is weak evidence: F14 shows Victoria Street at band 3 (20–29 km/h), not band 1/2, and F16 records no incidents, so RD-4-style congestion justification is unavailable and the statement in F13 is unsupported by the traffic facts.

Under NS-2 the fee refund is mandatory, and the driver's profile (F19: 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 d) makes an additional account flag under NS-2's second branch available if the judge characterises the 08:16 "I'm Here" tap as an abuse of the arrival button — a risk I cannot fully rebut from the fact table.

points.response: The tap at 08:16:00 (F5) does satisfy NS-1(i) as a bare button press, so I do not contest that element — but a tap made 613 m from the pickup with 0 s inside 200 m afterwards cannot satisfy (ii) or (iii), so NS-1 as a whole still fails (F5, F1).
This concedes my C1/C2: the tap was made 613 m away (F5) and the platform recorded no arrival at all (F4), so the arrival prerequisite of NS-1(ii) is unmet.
This concedes my C3: 0 s inside 200 m after the tap and a closest approach of 612 m (F5, F1) mean there was no continuous 3-minute wait at the pickup under NS-1(iii).
Agreed, and it disposes of the case in the rider's favour: NS-2 mandates refund_full of the $6.61 recorded in F3/F6; NS-7 only governs the voucher form of that refund and does not reduce it.

Stopping still 613 m away for 6 min 20 s (F2) proves only that the car was parked, not that the driver was at the pickup point; the fix he held at is 613 m from the Victoria St entrance (F2, F5), so this supports the rider, not an NS-1 defence.

This is the driver's own concession that F13 is unsupported: Victoria Street at band 3 (F14) is not the band 1/2 severe congestion RD-4 requires, and F16 shows no incidents, so nothing excuses parking 613 m away and tapping "I'm Here".

The complete, timestamped chat (F12) is precisely what shows the rider was waiting at the named entrance (F8, F10) while the driver's 08:16 "I'm here already" (F9) was false against GPS (F5) — the system record wins, so NS-2 governs and the fee falls.
I agree no SAFE-1 escalation is required; my brief never alleged a threat, harassment or dangerous driving, and F11 is a plain cancellation notice (F11).

Conceded in substance: F5 shows the 08:16:00 "I'm Here" tap was made 613 m from the pickup, outside any plausible arrival radius, and F1/F4 confirm the driver never reached the point the platform would record as the pick-up location — this is exactly the D2 finding in my own brief.
